previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with poorly controlled type 1 diabetes was admitted after being found unresponsive at home with a blood glucose of 40. She had been discharged the prior day following treatment for diabetic ketoacidosis. Altered mental status was attributed to hypoglycemia, exacerbated by irregular eating habits and insulin use. A central line was placed for access, and she developed coagulase-negative staphylococcal bacteremia, likely line-associated, requiring a PICC line and a 14-day course of intravenous vancomycin. Her blood sugars remained labile initially but stabilized with the initiation of Lantus insulin and fixed-dose Humalog with meals. Acute kidney injury resolved with hydration, and anemia was monitored without transfusion. She was discharged home with nursing support for IV antibiotics, clear instructions on insulin management, and follow-up plans for vascular surgery due to dry gangrene and ongoing diabetes care.
